Sushi originated in Southeast Asia over 2,000 years ago as a way to preserve fish by fermenting it with rice.
In the 8th century, sushi evolved into the form we know today when Japanese cooks began to add vinegar to the rice used in sushi.
Sushi became popular in Japan during the Edo period (1603-1868) when street vendors began to sell small portions of sushi wrapped in seaweed.
The style of sushi known as nigiri became synonymous with the dish.
Japanese immigrants brought sushi to the United States in the late 1800s.
Sushi became popular in the Western world in the 1960s and 70s when sushi restaurants began to open in major cities such as New York and San Francisco.
Today, sushi is enjoyed around the world and has evolved to include a wide variety of ingredients and techniques.
